items.evidence: horizon-items/src/items.rs LootContext::condition() reads the kind ONLY from o.get("type"); 1.21.7 conditions use the "condition" key, so kind is "" and the match falls to _ => false. The plural "conditions" array IS consulted — every element fails. Path verified end to end (Game::block_loot_at -> block_drops_by_player -> evaluate -> conditions -> condition), no fallback or normalisation in the load path. 961/1,023 block tables carry >=1 condition; 1,006/1,246 tables overall. Owner-confirmed in-game 2026-11-22 ("survival block-breaking drops nothing"). The 26.2 tree has the fix (o.get("type").or_else(|| o.get("condition"))); 1.21.7 lacks it. Note: items.rs function dispatch (line 2277) already has the .or(f["function"]) fix — only conditions are broken here.
items.title: Block drops evaluate every loot condition as false; survival block-breaking drops nothing

items.evidence: horizon-world/src/loot.rs is written for the 26.x loot format: pools/entries/modifiers consulted via singular "condition" (lines 2018/2071/1488) while 1.21.7 uses plural "conditions" (never evaluated, every entry passes); condition() reads c["type"] while 1.21.7 uses "condition"; run() reads f["type"] while 1.21.7 uses "function", default arm _ => {} (every function a silent no-op). RAN loot_fill on mob-spawn/resources, seeds 1-5: blocks/stone -> minecraft:stone (silk-touch child wins unconditionally; vanilla drops cobblestone), blocks/diamond_ore -> minecraft:diamond_ore (vanilla: diamond), chests/simple_dungeon -> every stack count 1 (set_count ignored). Affects entity drops, chest/container loot, fishing, trial spawners, vaults: 1,006 tables carry conditions, 327 carry functions, 1,115 at least one. No fortune, no looting, no explosion decay, no killed_by_player/random_chance gating. The 26.2 tree has all three halves of the fix; 1.21.7 has none.
items.method: code trace + loot_fill run on real data
items.title: The loot.rs engine ignores all loot conditions and all loot functions

items.evidence: crafting.rs Recipes::from_sources. (a) 8 handled specials dropped: 1.21.7's special files are bare {"type", "category"} (ingredients live in vanilla Java code) but the parser requires JSON ingredient/result fields, so parse returns None: banner duplicate, shield decoration, book cloning, firework rocket, firework star, firework star fade, map extending, decorated pot. Only repairitem loads (needs no fields). Bare form also verified in 1.21.6/1.21.10 named jars — likely all E6 versions. (b) 3 specials have no parser arm at all (26.x type names only): crafting_special_armordye (parser: crafting_dye), crafting_special_tippedarrow (parser: crafting_imbue), crafting_special_mapcloning (26.x does it as transmute; 1.21.7's 32 transmutes are bundle/shulker dyeing only). No other Special construction site exists. All other types load: shaped 673, shapeless 295, cooking 114, transmute 32, stonecutting 254 + smithing 27 (via stations.rs), repairitem 1.
items.method: parser arms vs jar recipe files
items.title: 11 of 12 special recipes never load (parser knows only the 26.x special-recipe form)

items.evidence: horizon-client-core/src/potions.rs EFFECTS has 40 entries vs vanilla 1.21.7's 39; the extra is breath_of_the_nautilus (colour 65518, Beneficial), absent from the jar's registry dump and MobEffects class. Appended last, so the 39 vanilla protocol ids are unaffected (order verified vs registries.json protocol ids 0-38). All 39 vanilla colours, categories and instant flags verified against javap -c on MobEffects.<clinit> (instant exactly: instant_health, instant_damage, saturation — HealOrHarmMobEffect/SaturationMobEffect extend InstantenousMobEffect).
items.title: Port's MobEffects table carries a 26.x-only effect (breath_of_the_nautilus)

items.evidence: crafting.rs Ingredient::parse_object requires a neoforge:ingredient_type or type key and returns None otherwise, so vanilla object forms ({"item": "..."}, {"tag": "..."}) fail to parse and the recipe is dropped. No vanilla 1.21.7 recipe uses object ingredients (all 3,239 ingredient slots are plain strings), so this affects only player datapack / mod recipes using the object form.
items.title: Object-form recipe ingredients are rejected (datapack scope only)

The 1.21.7 jar itself ships tags/block/mineable/{axe,hoe,pickaxe,shovel}.json, the prepared copies are byte-identical, and no rename code exists in the 1.21.7 tree. Boundaries kept: enchantment effect VALUES and advancement criterion CONDITION semantics belong to other batches (wiring verified here, values not); recipe-book display of the 11 dropped specials not checked; registries.json minecraft:block_type (255 entries, unverified provenance) not used for any count or check.
source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 12 — recipes (1,407), loot tables (1,246), advancements (1,520, triggers only), tags (589), enchantments (42), status effects (39), damage types (49). Vanilla spec: 1.21.7-server-named.jar data/ + javap on MobEffects; port data: versions/1.21.7/.local/horizon-client/1.21.7/data/minecraft/ (identical to mob-spawn/resources/). Checks only, no fixes.
systemic_note: The prepared data is faithful — all 4,853 data-driven files byte-identical to the 1.21.7 jar, block-tags.json byte-faithful too. Every defect is code reading the 26.x form of a format 1.21.7 writes differently and failing silently: loot condition/function keys (B12-G01/G02), special-recipe form and type names (B12-G03), a 26.x effect in the table (B12-G04). Same bug class as the pilot's 26.x-tag findings (G1/G3/G5/G6), one level down. The 26.2 playtest fix for the loot half was never carried to 1.21.7 (and only half-carried to items.rs: functions yes, conditions no).
